Method of Attack: Harvesting credit card details and personal information via a fake McAfee subscription renewal scam page
Collecting visitor's name, email, card number, expiration date, CVC, address, city, state, zip, and phone number through forms
Redirecting users to a thank you page with a phone number to call for fake technical support
Scammers remotely connect to victim's computer and claim credit card info did not go through, pushing affiliate sales
Distributing adware that creates random executables to open advertising redirects promoting adult sites, fake blogs, unwanted chrome extensions, and adware downloads
Discoverer: Thomas Roccia, security researcher at McAfee Labs
Impacted Systems: Windows PCs infected by WizzCaster adware
Attack Vector: Browser-based scam page mimicking McAfee subscription expiration
Phishing forms on scam website onlineav-shop.com
Remote desktop connection initiated by scammers after victim calls provided phone number
Adware installed on infected PCs that auto-starts and opens malicious advertisements
Indicators of Compromise: Affiliate URLs used by scammers to generate commissions
Malware hashes identified as WizzCaster adware
Behavior of random named executables auto-starting on login
Advertising redirects promoting adult sites, fake blogs, unwanted chrome extensions, and adware downloads
